calls.body: The Flyers hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t. Philadelphia is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Flyers.

surprises.head: Dan Vladař stole one
surprises.body: Vladař allowed 1 goal on 28 shots, worth 3.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than Philadelphia’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

story.head: Vladař stands on his head
paras: The Sabres’ Jason Zucker played his first game of the season, after missing the first nine. Cole Knuble, in his second NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Oliver Bonk, late in the first to open the scoring for the Flyers. Trevor Zegras made it 2-0 on the power play four and a half minutes later, and that one stood up as the winner. Zucker got the Sabres on the board on the power play late in the second, but that was as close as they got. Knuble scored again early in the third to make it 3-1 for the Flyers, and Hunter McDonald and Mattias Samuelsson dropped the gloves late in the period.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Dan Vladař made 27 saves for the Flyers, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 23 of 26.

Samuelsson was thrown out with a game misconduct late in the third. The Sabres killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a little over a minute late in the second. The Flyers moved to 3-6-3, and the Sabres fell to 4-4-2.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Flyers.
Noah Cates’s five-game point streak against Buffalo ended.
Jack Quinn extended his point streak against Philadelphia to six games.
Michael Bunting was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Tyson Foerster played instead.
